implement.summary:
DRAFT FOR QUALIFIED ATTORNEY REVIEW — NOT LEGAL ADVICE

LIQUIDATED DAMAGES CALCULATION MEMORANDUM

Jurisdiction and governing law
England and Wales is assumed, based on the sterling figures in the instruction. The contract itself was not provided. A rule stated here is not assumed to hold in any other jurisdiction.

Contract terms applied (as given in the request)
- Liquidated damages rate: £1,250 for each day after 14 March.
- Contractual completion date / LD trigger: 14 March (same year).
- Date of completion of the works: 29 April (same year).
- Contract price: £480,000.
- Cap: 10% of the contract price.

Day count (ask 3)
The clause charges LDs "for each day after 14 March". 14 March is therefore not a chargeable delay day. Chargeable days run from 15 March through 29 April inclusive (the date the works were completed).

Count:
- Remaining days in March after 14 March: 31 − 14 = 17 days (15–31 March).
- Days in April up to and including 29 April: 29 days.
- Total: 17 + 29 = 46 days.

Cross-check by date difference: 29 April minus 14 March = 46 calendar days. Cross-check by day-of-year (February lies before the period, so leap/non-leap does not change the result): 14 March is day 73 (non-leap) / 74 (leap); 29 April is day 119 (non-leap) / 120 (leap); difference = 46 in both cases.

Weekends and holidays are included. The request does not state a working-days-only convention, so calendar days are used.

Uncapped amount (ask 4)
46 days × £1,250 per day = £57,500.

Cap
10% × £480,000 = £48,000.

Does the cap apply? (ask 2)
Yes. The uncapped accrual of £57,500 exceeds the £48,000 cap. The cap binds.

Liquidated damages payable (ask 1)
£48,000 (the capped amount). The excess of £57,500 − £48,000 = £9,500 is not payable under the cap.

Summary of figures
| Item                  | Amount / count |
|-----------------------|----------------|
| Days counted          | 46             |
| Daily rate            | £1,250         |
| Uncapped LDs          | £57,500        |
| Cap (10% of £480,000) | £48,000        |
| Cap applies?          | Yes            |
| LDs payable           | £48,000        |

Caveats for reviewing attorney (not answered as separate asks)
This calculation applies the figures and wording supplied. It does not opine on: (a) whether the clause is an enforceable liquidated damages provision or a penalty under the law of England and Wales; (b) whether any extension of time moved the 14 March trigger; (c) whether any variation changed the £480,000 contract price and therefore the 10% cap base; (d) whether notice, certification or other contractual conditions precedent to deduction or recovery of LDs were satisfied; (e) VAT, interest or rounding (whole pounds, no VAT or interest, have been assumed); or (f) whether the governing law is in fact England and Wales. Those points require the executed contract and instructions.
